problem: Let $a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -3 \\ 4\end{aligned}]$ and $b=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Find the orthogonal projection of $a$ onto $\text{Span}{b}.$

feedback.problem: Let $a=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ -1 \\ 5\end{aligned}]$ and $b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Find the orthogonal projection of $a$ onto $\text{Span}{b}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The orthogonal projection of $a$ onto $\text{Span}{b}$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,a & =\frac{b\cdot a}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{1\cdot 2+1\cdot 2+0\cdot (-1)+1\cdot 5}{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{2+2+0+5}{1+1+0+1}b \\  & =\frac{9}{3}b \\  & =3b \\  & =3[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
